name: New Year's Day
description: New Year's Day marks the beginning of a new calendar year. It is traditionally celebrated with fireworks, countdowns, parties, and gatherings with family and friends.
details: January 1 is the first day of the Gregorian calendar. In the United States, it is a federal holiday when government offices close and many businesses operate on reduced hours.

name: Martin Luther King Jr. Day
description: Martin Luther King Jr. Day honors the life and legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., a major leader of the American civil rights movement.
details: Dr. King advocated nonviolent protest and equal rights for African Americans. The day is also recognized as a National Day of Service, encouraging people to volunteer and help their communities.

name: Washington's Birthday
description: Washington's Birthday honors George Washington, the first President of the United States and a central figure in the country's founding.
details: The holiday is commonly called Presidents Day, although its official federal name remains Washington's Birthday. It is celebrated on the third Monday of February.

name: Memorial Day
description: Memorial Day honors American military personnel who died while serving in the United States Armed Forces.
details: People remember fallen service members through memorial ceremonies, visits to cemeteries, and the placement of flags on graves. It is also commonly considered the unofficial beginning of summer in the United States.

name: Juneteenth National Independence Day
description: Juneteenth commemorates the end of slavery in the United States, particularly the announcement of freedom to enslaved people in Galveston, Texas, in 1865.
details: On June 19, 1865, Union troops arrived in Galveston and announced that enslaved people were free, more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation. Celebrations often include cultural events, music, food, and educational activities.

name: Independence Day
description: Independence Day celebrates the adoption of the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776, when the American colonies declared their independence from Great Britain.
details: The holiday is widely celebrated with fireworks, parades, concerts, barbecues, and patriotic displays. In 2026, July 4 falls on Saturday, so the federal holiday is observed on Friday, July 3.

name: Labor Day
description: Labor Day recognizes the contributions and achievements of American workers and the labor movement.
details: The holiday celebrates workers' role in building the country's economy and improving working conditions. It is observed on the first Monday of September and is often considered the unofficial end of summer.

name: Columbus Day
description: Columbus Day commemorates Christopher Columbus's 1492 arrival in the Americas.
details: The holiday has a complicated history and is viewed differently across the United States. Some communities celebrate Indigenous Peoples' Day instead, recognizing the histories and cultures of Native American and Indigenous communities.

name: Veterans Day
description: Veterans Day honors all people who have served in the United States Armed Forces, including living and deceased veterans.
details: The date originally marked the end of World War I, when the armistice took effect on November 11, 1918. Today, ceremonies, parades, and recognition events are held to thank military veterans for their service.

details: Many American families celebrate with roast turkey, stuffing, mashed potatoes, pumpkin pie, and other traditional dishes. It is observed on the fourth Thursday of November and is followed by the major shopping day known as Black Friday.
